citations.B1: Read-then-write on `counts[user_id]` races across threads — two requests can both pass the check and both increment, overrunning the limit
citations.B3: use a lock or atomic/CAS structure
citations.B4: No time window — once a user hits `limit`, they're blocked forever; add a sliding/fixed window with expiry
citations.B5: `counts` dict grows unboundedly, one entry per user forever — evict or expire old entries
citations.B6: Not process-safe for multi-worker deployment (e.g. gunicorn workers) since each process has its own `counts`
citations.B7: No input validation on `user_id` (None, empty, non-hashable)
